title: Atlantis
summary: Atlantis is a legendary sunken city submerged beneath the waters of Greece. Historically constructed by the ancient Atlanteans under the guidance of the Casterwill Family, the city serves as a heavily fortified sanctuary and the ultimate resting place of the legendary Amulet of Will. The city is structurally protected from the crushing deep-sea environment by a massive, ancient magical atmospheric bubble. This perimeter barrier keeps the city completely dry and allows human Seekers to breathe normally. The primary entryway to the sunken continent is hidden on the surface, concealed beneath the ruins of the Temple of Poseidon.

sections.heading: History
sections.wikitext:
In the modern era, the [[Eathon Lambert's puzzle|puzzle]] required to unlock the final vault mechanism inside the lower levels of the compound was successfully recovered by the legendary Seeker [[Eathon Lambert]]. {{Source|S1E15}} Eathon journeyed to Atlantis where he singehandedly fought a huge battle with [[the Professor's Personal Guard]]. However he never made it to the Casterwill compound. {{Source|S1E21}}

Ten years later, Eathon's son Lok Lambert brought the puzzle back to Atlantis. He and the Huntik team took on the trials of Atlantis and managed to pass four tests. Shortly after, the city was breached by the [[Organization]], and Lok used his authorized master command over the Atlantis Guardian to ambush [[Rassimov]] and his team of [[Suits]], weaponizing the facility's defenses in a defensive rage after discovering his father had never safely arrived at the sanctuary. Following the battle, by successfully inserting the key and decoding the central altar puzzle, Lok manged to retrieve the Amulet of Will. {{source|S1E21}}

sections.heading: Layout and Architecture
sections.wikitext:
The design of Atlantis relies heavily on sacred geometry dedicated to the Greek god of the sea. The layout consists of two primary zones:
* '''The Six Temples''': The city features a strict radial defensive architecture. Four distinct temples anchor the four cardinal corners of the city, while a fifth temple sits directly behind the central Casterwill stronghold. The ruined Temple of Poseidon on the surface acts as the sixth and final anchor point.
* '''The Casterwill Compound''': One of the last intact bastions of the First Seeker's bloodline, this compound holds ancient archives and the main vault chamber. The entire complex is shielded by an [[Atlantis Guardian|autonomous defensive enchantment]] that restricts entry strictly to those who prove their worth.

full_text:
Atlantis is a legendary sunken city submerged beneath the waters of Greece. Historically constructed by the ancient Atlanteans under the guidance of the Casterwill Family, the city serves as a heavily fortified sanctuary and the ultimate resting place of the legendary Amulet of Will. The city is structurally protected from the crushing deep-sea environment by a massive, ancient magical atmospheric bubble. This perimeter barrier keeps the city completely dry and allows human Seekers to breathe normally. The primary entryway to the sunken continent is hidden on the surface, concealed beneath the ruins of the Temple of Poseidon.

== History ==
In the modern era, the puzzle required to unlock the final vault mechanism inside the lower levels of the compound was successfully recovered by the legendary Seeker Eathon Lambert. [S1E15] Eathon journeyed to Atlantis where he singehandedly fought a huge battle with the Professor's Personal Guard. However he never made it to the Casterwill compound. [S1E21]

Ten years later, Eathon's son Lok Lambert brought the puzzle back to Atlantis. He and the Huntik team took on the trials of Atlantis and managed to pass four tests. Shortly after, the city was breached by the Organization, and Lok used his authorized master command over the Atlantis Guardian to ambush Rassimov and his team of Suits, weaponizing the facility's defenses in a defensive rage after discovering his father had never safely arrived at the sanctuary. Following the battle, by successfully inserting the key and decoding the central altar puzzle, Lok manged to retrieve the Amulet of Will. [S1E21]

== Layout and Architecture ==
The design of Atlantis relies heavily on sacred geometry dedicated to the Greek god of the sea. The layout consists of two primary zones:
* The Six Temples: The city features a strict radial defensive architecture. Four distinct temples anchor the four cardinal corners of the city, while a fifth temple sits directly behind the central Casterwill stronghold. The ruined Temple of Poseidon on the surface acts as the sixth and final anchor point.
* The Casterwill Compound: One of the last intact bastions of the First Seeker's bloodline, this compound holds ancient archives and the main vault chamber. The entire complex is shielded by an autonomous defensive enchantment that restricts entry strictly to those who prove their worth.

== The Trials of Atlantis ==
To bypass the magical ward sealing the Casterwill Compound, an intruder or Seeker must successfully overcome four consecutive elemental and psychological tests designed to filter out the unworthy.

=== The Trial of Bravery ===
* Challenger: Lok Lambert
* The Test: The Seeker must deliberately walk through a roaring, intense wall of mystical flames. 
* Outcome: Passed. The fire behaves as an illusion that inflicts absolutely no physical harm, provided the challenger maintains unwavering resolve and shows zero fear.

=== The Trial of Prowess ===
* Challenger: Dante Vale
* The Test: A martial combat trial requiring the Seeker to defeat three aquatic Mermen gladiators. The chamber is heavily enchanted with a direct mimicry hex: whenever the challenger invokes a Titan, the chamber automatically manifests an Atlantean counterpart of identical power (such as matching Metagolem with a Coralgolem, or Caliban with Caliban Ocean Warrior).
* Outcome: Passed. Dante bypassed the mirror mechanic by invoking Behemoth, the Legendary Titan of Body. Because Legendary Titans possess no equivalent, the chamber failed to generate a counterpart and their attempt backfired - badly.

=== The Trial of Intelligence ===
* Challenger: Sophie Casterwill
* The Test: A riddle of architectural history demanding the exact number of temples built by the Atlanteans to honor Poseidon.
* Outcome: Passed. Sophie correctly answered "six" — deducing that the total included the four corner city temples, the inner compound temple, and the ruined terrestrial surface temple.

=== The Trial of Nobility ===
* Challenger: Zhalia Moon
* The Test: A spiritual and psychological evaluation forcing the challenger to demonstrate genuine inner integrity and absolute self-honesty.
* Outcome: Passed. Zhalia successfully broke the trial by openly admitting her past deceptive crimes and confronting her deepest personal guilt.
